items.text: Claude GitHub App installed on ck5o4/multifamily with write access - cloud push unblocked
items.why: FIXED 2026-08-17 by Anthony. Root cause was subtler than 'a missing scope': the Claude app was AUTHORIZED on ck5o4 but INSTALLED only on the flux-brain-hq org, never on the personal account that owns multifamily. Authorization is what let cloud sessions read; installation is what grants repo Contents:write, so every push 403'd while every read succeeded - exactly the observed asymmetry. Installed via github.com/apps/claude/installations/new -> ck5o4 -> Only select repositories -> multifamily. Verified at installation 154488689: 'Read and write access to ... code' and 'Selected 1 repository: ck5o4/multifamily'. Scoped to that one repo deliberately. NOTE: the post-install redirect lands on claude.ai/admin-settings/... which shows 'You don't have access to organization settings' on a personal plan - that dead end is cosmetic, not a failure. CONFIRMED 2026-08-18 PM: the scheduled cloud sweep pushed to origin/main for real (3254356..feb4e3a). No 403, no recovery-patch email. TRAP FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: the cloud container starts on a DETACHED HEAD with the local 'main' ref left at a stale commit, so 'git push -u origin main' fails with 'behind its remote' and reads exactly like the old permissions failure. It is not. Fix is 'git branch -f main HEAD && git checkout main' before pushing, or push HEAD:main. SECOND HALF OF THE TRAP, found 2026-08-18: the stale ref is not just local 'main' - the remote-tracking ref 'origin/main' is ALSO stale on container start. This run opened with 'git log origin/main..HEAD' listing 9 commits that looked unpushed (including work already confirmed pushed on 08-18 PM). They were not unpushed; the container's cached origin/main simply predated them. A single 'git fetch origin main' moved origin/main ccdf19f..f38b13b and the list went empty. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUTINE: step 4 tells the scan to judge the git-push-rule todo by whether 'git log origin/main..HEAD' is empty, so ALWAYS fetch before running that test - otherwise a clean repo reads as 9 commits of lost work and the scan will 'recover' work that was never lost.

items.text: Pin openpyxl in the environment setup for scheduled cloud runs
items.why: openpyxl is absent in every fresh cloud container. Without it tools/board.py replaces BOTH live deal cards (Eden, Treme) with 'could not compute' placeholders and the board drops from ~17KB to ~10.8KB; it does print ERRORS, so it is not silent. requirements.txt was written into a container working tree 2026-08-15 but could not reach the repo because of the push 403, so it recurs every run. CREATED FOR REAL in the repo by the local session 2026-08-17 - this closes once the cloud setup step installs from it. Local machine is unaffected (openpyxl 3.1.5 present). RECURRED 2026-08-18 scan: absent again in the fresh container, and it blocks MORE than the board - tools/test_pymodel.py imports openpyxl at line 19 and died on import, so the health step could not run at all until it was installed. WORKAROUND CONFIRMED THIS RUN: 'pip install -r requirements.txt' succeeds inside the container (pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org are on the proxy noProxy bypass list, so PyPI is reachable even though FRED is not). After installing, all three suites ran and the board rendered full-size at 24,987 bytes. So the fix is purely to add that one install line to the cloud setup step; nothing in the repo needs to change. RECURRED AGAIN 2026-08-19 (third consecutive cloud scan: 08-17, 08-18, 08-19). Same signature: tools/test_pymodel.py and tools/test_regressions.py both died at 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named openpyxl' before running a single assertion; tools/test_mc.py passed because it does not import openpyxl. 'pip3 install -r requirements.txt' fixed it again in ~10 seconds, after which all three suites passed and board.py rendered 27,359 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Nothing in the repo needs changing - requirements.txt is correct and committed. The one-line fix remains: add 'pip install -r requirements.txt' to the cloud environment setup step. RECURRED A FOURTH TIME 2026-08-20 (08-17, 08-18, 08-19, 08-20). Identical signature: test_pymodel.py died at openpyxl import line 19, test_regressions.py died at pymodel._load_deal openpyxl import; test_mc.py passed. 'pip3 install -q -r requirements.txt' fixed it in seconds, then all three suites passed and board.py rendered 29,307 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Still the same one-line setup fix. RECURRED A FIFTH TIME 2026-08-21 (08-17, 08-18, 08-19, 08-20, 08-21). Identical signature: tools/test_pymodel.py died at 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named openpyxl' (import line 19) before a single assertion ran; test_mc.py passed because it does not import openpyxl. 'pip install -r requirements.txt' fixed it in seconds (openpyxl 3.1.5 + et-xmlfile 2.0.0), after which all three suites passed and board.py rendered 30,721 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Five consecutive scans, same one-line setup fix, nothing in the repo needs changing. RECURRED 2026-08-22: absent again in the fresh container — tools/test_pymodel.py died at the line-19 import before any test ran. 'pip3 install -r requirements.txt' fixed it in-container again and the board then wrote 32,819 bytes (full cards, not the ~10.8KB degraded fallback). Five straight runs now start with this manual step; the cloud setup step still does not install from requirements.txt. RECURRED A SEVENTH TIME 2026-08-23 (08-17 through 08-23, every consecutive cloud scan). Identical signature: tools/test_pymodel.py died at 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named openpyxl' (import line 19) and tools/test_regressions.py died at the same import inside pymodel._load_deal, both before a single assertion ran; test_mc.py passed because it does not import openpyxl. 'pip3 install -r requirements.txt' fixed it in seconds (openpyxl 3.1.5 + et-xmlfile 2.0.0), after which all three suites passed and board.py rendered 33,993 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Nothing in the repo needs changing; the one-line fix is still to add 'pip install -r requirements.txt' to the cloud environment setup step. | DONE 2026-08-24: SessionStart hook installs requirements.txt on remote runs (.claude/hooks/session-start.sh). VERIFIED FIXED 2026-08-24 (first cloud scan after the hook landed): openpyxl 3.1.5 was present at container start with NO manual pip install — the .claude/hooks/session-start.sh SessionStart hook installed requirements.txt before the scan ran. All three suites executed from a cold container (test_pymodel 4/4 deals PASS, test_mc 79 passed, test_regressions all passed) and board.py rendered 33,361 bytes with both live deal cards intact. Eight-run recurrence (08-17 through 08-23) is broken. Stays done. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-25 (second cloud scan after the hook landed): openpyxl present at container start with no manual pip install; all three suites ran from cold (test_pymodel 4/4 deals PASS, test_mc 79 passed, test_regressions all passed) and board.py rendered 36,715 bytes with both live deal cards intact — not the ~10.8KB degraded fallback. The hook is holding. Stays done.

items.text: Allow fred.stlouisfed.org and the comp websites in the CLOUD environment network policy
items.why: CLOUD-ONLY - scoped correctly 2026-08-17. In cloud containers the egress proxy returns 403 CONNECT for fred.stlouisfed.org (killing tools/rates.py with 'curl exit 56') and for parcatdenhamsprings.com and springtreedenham.com (killing the marketwatch snapshot). Both ran CLEAN from the local machine on 2026-08-17 - rates: WSJ Prime 6.75 pct, 10yr 4.68 pct, SOFR 3.62 pct, no drift vs defaults.py; marketwatch: snapshot 2026-08-17 saved, all four properties OK. So the scan is not broken, it is only broken unattended. Until the policy is fixed, rates and marketwatch must be run locally. HARD EVIDENCE 2026-08-18: the proxy's own status endpoint now names the failure explicitly - curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status reports recentRelayFailures kind 'connect_rejected', detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', host 'fred.stlouisfed.org:443'. Both FRED hostnames are blocked (fred.stlouisfed.org AND api.stlouisfed.org), each returning 'curl (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. IMPORTANT NUANCE: do NOT read 'the container has no network' - PyPI installs work fine because pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org sit on the proxy noProxy bypass list. This is a per-host allowlist, so the fix is to add fred.stlouisfed.org, api.stlouisfed.org, parcatdenhamsprings.com and springtreedenham.com to the ENVIRONMENT's network policy (the environment was created with a restricted egress policy; see code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web). Rates have now gone unverified in cloud on 08-17 and 08-18 - the 6.75 pct Prime in defaults.py is carried from the 08-17 LOCAL run, not confirmed today. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-19, still blocked, now THREE consecutive cloud scans without verified rates (08-17, 08-18, 08-19). tools/rates.py died identically at 'FRED unreachable for DPRIME: curl exit 56'; the proxy status endpoint again logged recentRelayFailures kind 'connect_rejected', detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', host 'fred.stlouisfed.org:443' (two entries, 2026-08-19T14:15Z). Per /root/.ccr/README.md a 403 from the proxy is an org egress-policy denial that must be reported, not retried or routed around, so this run did not attempt a workaround. CONSEQUENCE: the 6.75 pct WSJ Prime in defaults.py has now been carried unverified for 2 days beyond its 2026-08-17 local confirmation. It is not known to be wrong - it is simply unchecked. Verify locally before pricing any deal. Two mitigating facts found this run: (a) the empty snapshot dir is untracked by git (git does not track empty directories), so it never reaches the repo and cannot masquerade as a fresh snapshot for the next scan — the only durable record is four ok:false rows appended to market-data/observations.jsonl dated 2026-08-24; (b) 'marketwatch.py report' is robust to the failed day, still diffing 08-08 vs 08-17 and producing no false 'everything leased' signal. Probed four other public rate hosts through the proxy and ALL returned the same 403 CONNECT: home.treasury.gov, fiscaldata.treasury.gov, api.stlouisfed.org, www.federalreserve.gov. So this is a strict per-host ALLOWLIST, not a FRED-specific denial. Do NOT spend effort rewriting tools/rates.py against Treasury or the Fed as a workaround — those hosts are blocked identically. The ONLY fix is adding the hosts to the environment's network policy. items.text: Pull asking price + unit count on the unscreenable NOLA listings (2 open): 929 Monterey Ct, Gretna (12 units, needs price); and 1510 Louisiana Ave, Uptown New Orleans 70115 (4 units, needs a VERIFIED price and condition). 3260 Kabel Dr is RESOLVED DEAD 2026-09-02 - do not re-pull it.
items.why: NEW 2026-08-17. Twelve alerts piled up 08-05 to 08-16 while nobody read the digests, and the sweeps listed addresses without ever assigning verdicts. Full triage now in deal-intake/_pipeline/triage-2026-08-17.md. Resolved without Crexi by reading unit counts out of the alert email bodies: 7 dead on geography, S. Genois dead at 2 units, Gentilly Ridge dead at 92 units (~$2M+ equity vs ~$300K available). Gretna is the ONE survivor - 12 units in Jefferson, same profile as Baker, needs only a price. Lafayette W Congress needs price AND unit count. Apply the NOLA overlay when screening Gretna: Jefferson millage 118.40, insurance $3,000/unit for wind, flood.py mandatory. ADDED 2026-09-01 (evening sweep): 3260 Kabel Drive, New Orleans 70131 (Algiers, Orleans Parish, West Bank) folded in here and its CHECK item retired under the two-digest rule. It was carried as an unresolved CHECK in the 09-01 AM and PM digests; this run tried to resolve it and could not. Reason, stated rather than assumed: the Crexi alert body for this listing contains ONLY the street address - no price and no unit count - unlike the 08-05..08-16 alerts whose bodies embedded unit counts and let the 08-17 triage kill seven listings without opening Crexi. The listing page itself needs a logged-in Crexi session, which an unattended sweep does not have, and no repo tool derives units or price from an address (parceltax.py takes the assessment as an INPUT, it does not fetch it). So Kabel Dr is NOT screened and must not be reported as either live or dead: it is in-box on geography (Orleans metro) and unknown on everything else. Apply the NOLA overlay when it is finally screened: Orleans millage 131.99, insurance $3,000/unit for wind, flood.py mandatory, and Algiers is Zone X only behind West Bank levee protection - say the residual risk out loud. STANDING NOTE FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: Crexi has stopped embedding unit counts in these alert bodies, so the 08-17 read-the-body triage trick no longer works and every new Crexi alert will land unscreenable. Do not keep spawning CHECK items that no unattended run can close - park them here. KABEL DR RESOLVED 2026-09-02 PM (email sweep) - and the 09-01 'every new Crexi alert will land unscreenable' note is TOO STRONG, so do not treat it as a rule. The Crexi alert body still carries only the street address, but the listing is public outside Crexi: a plain web search on the address returned MLS #2571572 with the asking price, unit count and gross income, no login required. SCREEN RESULT for 3260 Kabel Dr, New Orleans 70131 (Algiers, Orleans): ask $589,000, 4 units, all 2BR/1.5BA, fully occupied, new roof, separately metered electric and water, gross scheduled income $4,245/mo = $50,940/yr, i.e. $147,250/unit against $1,061 rents. Hand screen on the house Orleans overlay (7% vacancy; Orleans millage 131.99 on 10% of $589K = ~$7,774 tax; insurance $3,000/unit = $12,000; mgmt 8% of EGI; R&M/G&A/mktg/other per unit per CLAUDE.md; utilities cut to ~$300/unit for separate meters; capex $250/unit; payroll $0 under 20 units) gives NOI ~$15,550 on EGI ~$47,374 - a 2.6% cap at ask. Debt service at 75% LTV/~7%/25yr is ~$37,500, so DSCR ~0.41 against a house floor of 1.30. To clear 1.30 DSCR the price would have to fall to roughly $190K, a 68% cut. VERDICT: DEAD - not a price negotiation, an order-of-magnitude miss. Caveat stated rather than hidden: this is a screen off PUBLIC LISTING DATA, not a seller T-12 or rent roll, so the expense lines are house assumptions; the verdict does not turn on their precision. No deal-intake folder created - nothing to ingest. LESSON FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: before parking a Crexi alert as unscreenable, try a public web search on the street address; MLS syndication sites carry price and unit count that the alert body omits. Note the Coldwell Banker and similar listing pages are themselves EGRESS_BLOCKED in cloud (add to the network-policy host list if direct fetches are wanted), but the search result snippets carried enough to screen this one. ADDED 2026-09-04 PM (email sweep): 1510 Louisiana Ave, New Orleans 70115 (Uptown, Orleans) arrived as a Crexi saved-search alert at 19:45 UTC, titled 'Uptown Assemblage with Up to 45% Tax Credit Potential - Four Units with Ample Parking'. As always the alert body carried only the street address. Applied the 09-02 lesson recorded above and web-searched the address instead of parking it unscreenable - PARTIAL SUCCESS ONLY, and the failure is stated rather than papered over: two searches returned two DIFFERENT asking prices, $329,000 in one and $315,000 (Villere Realty, LLC) in the other, from synthesised search snippets rather than a listing page read directly. NEITHER IS VERIFIED and they must not be underwritten. What the range does tell us is directional and worth acting on: at $315-329K for 4 units that is ~$79-82K/unit in 70115, which is far below Uptown stabilised pricing. Combined with the '45% tax credit' framing (Louisiana historic rehab credits attach to REHABS, not stabilised assets) and the word 'Assemblage', the most likely readings are that the price covers the adjoining lot only, or that the building is a gut job. Either way this is a value-add/rehab play, NOT the stabilised first deal the buy box calls for. DO NOT underwrite on the estimated basis - the same trap already recorded on Treme. What is actually needed: the Crexi listing page (needs a logged-in session) or one call to the listing broker to confirm (a) what the price includes - building, lot, or both, (b) unit condition and whether any of the 4 units are currently rented, (c) whether the tax-credit claim is a real certified-rehab pathway or marketing. Apply the NOLA overlay when it is screened: Orleans millage 131.99, insurance $3,000/unit for wind, flood.py mandatory. Note also 70115 Uptown is largely Zone X behind levee protection - say the residual risk out loud rather than calling it clean.

items.text: St. Bernard Parish is IN the buy box - resolved by modelling, not by rule
items.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-17 by running the same 12-unit building through three parishes instead of arguing from millage. Price that clears 13%: Baker $528K (equity $146,520), Gretna $397K (equity $110,168), Chalmette $388K (equity $107,670). Chalmette vs Gretna is a $9,000 / 2.3% difference - noise. St. Bernard's heavier millage is NOT what moves the number. The $140K / 26.5% gap vs Baker is the METRO WIND INSURANCE ($3,000/unit vs $2,000), which hits Jefferson and Orleans identically. Conclusion: excluding St. Bernard while buying Gretna is incoherent - same deal, 2.3% apart. All three fit inside $300K capital comfortably, so capital is not the binding constraint on metro deals; the insurance quote is. Chalmette listing itself is Zone X shaded, NOT SFHA, so no lender-required flood policy - but that is post-Katrina levee protection, not natural safety, so price a voluntary policy.
